vikram: Heads up — since 02:30 UTC we've seen a bunch of Provisioner failures in ap-southeast1. GPU attach hangs with high iowait on local NVMe. Provisioner logs showing repeated attach retries.
carla: yeah saw the alert, here's the dashboard snapshot: https://dash.internal/r/graphs/ephemeral-iowait-ap-southeast1 :grimacing:
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu-provisioner.ap-southeast1.attach_fail_rate > 5% (rolling 15m)
sylvie_infra: quick summary from node telemetry: overlayfs fsync latency spiking, and /tmp inode count climbing. Not classic scrub spike — looks like a tempfile leak + heavy fsyncs from the recent image-puller change. dmesg shows repeated EIO on nvme0n1 at same offsets.
ethan: can you paste a couple lines of the dmesg/oom logs?
carla: logs excerpt: ```[ 1023.451234] nvme0n1: I/O 12345 qid 0 timeout, status 0x8
[ 1023.451258] overlayfs: __fuse_wait_timeout: fsync delayed for 2000ms
[ 1023.451300] kernel: unlinkat /tmp/app-XXXXX failed: ENOSPC```
vikram: df -h shows ephemeral partition near 99% on affected nodes. ``/tmp`` fill seems correlated with failed attach attempts (retries produce temp files).
sylvie_infra: root cause hypothesis: image-puller change created short-lived files but didn't close/ftruncate in error path -> kernel forced fsyncs and left lots of small files. Overlayfs handles metadata updates with extra fsyncs which amplifies NVMe IOPS.
zara_se: consequence: many GPU attach flows stall -> autoscaler sees nodes not ready -> we spin up more hosts which just hit same hot NVMe and increase cost. Seen 2x launch retries in last hour.
ethan: mitigation options? Can we gate the image-puller or throttle attach rate?
sylvie_infra: short-term mitigations we can do live (ordered by risk):
- pause image-puller rollout in ap-southeast1 (safe, immediate)
- temporarily increase janitor TTL for /tmp deletion frequency (aggressive cleanup)
- lower gpu-provisioner parallel attach concurrency in region (reduce retries)
- set IO cgroup throttle on image-puller service to 10MB/s to reduce fsync storm
- as last resort, cordon hotspot nodes and drain to force clean slate
carla: I can pause the rollout now. Doing it. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: ACTION: rollout/image-puller paused for ap-southeast1 by carla at 4861234578
vikram: please also push a one-off janitor run on the region. We need to reclaim free inodes ASAP.
sylvie_infra: one-off cleanup command (dry-run first): ```sudo find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type f -mmin +60 -print | head -n 200``` then if output looks sane: ```sudo find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type f -mmin +60 -delete``` DO NOT run on nodes serving customer long-lived workloads.
ethan: I'll queue a small canary to reduce attach concurrency to 2 in ap-southeast1 and watch. Patch ID: infra/attach-throttle#212 queued.
zara_se: cost note — every failed attach currently spins a new instance request which bills for 1-2 minutes before we kill it. If this continues for a few hours we could see ~10-15% spike in committed Dedicated spend for the region due to churn. Recommend throttling now.
carla: janitor run scheduled and started on 5 nodes that were at >95% used. reclaimed ~1.2GB and ~45k inodes each. attaching now looks better on those nodes.
sylvie_infra: next steps (short):
- revert image-puller change in staging and add extra close/ftruncate in error paths (PR up: https://git.internal/r/revert/image-puller-fix-486)
- add rate-limit to provisioner attach in region config (drop concurrency to 2-4)
- add short-term IO cgroup cap on image-puller systemd unit in ap-southeast1
- plan kernel patchback only if overlayfs fsync amplification still happens after app fix
ethan: can we add an SLO alert for inode consumption in ephemeral partitions? current alerts are just capacity/bytes.
sylvie_infra: yes, I'll add inode percentage alert for ap-southeast1 and eu-west as a follow-up. low-risk.
carla: devs rolling back the image-puller change in staging now. canary for prod tomorrow night after more tests.
ops-bot: NOTIFICATION: janitor reclaim completed on 5 nodes, avg reclaimed inodes=45k, reclaim_bytes=1.2GB
vikram: thanks team. Oncall runbook for this thread? ethan, can you paste a succinct checklist for pager coverage?
ethan: runbook bullets: 
1) check alert stream for attach_fail_rate
2) inspect df -i and df -h on top 5 affected nodes
3) pause image-puller rollout if inode% > 90%
4) run janitor find+delete dry-run, then delete on confirmed nodes
5) reduce provisioner attach concurrency and monitor queue depth
6) cordon/replace nodes as last resort
7) escalate to sylvie_infra if nvme EIOs persist after cleanup
zara_se: tagging billing@ for cost impact visibility.
carla: leaving notes in the incident doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/4861234567-ephemeral-fill-overlayfs-fsync-leak
sylvie_infra: I'll follow up with a postmortem once we verify staging rollback stops the pattern. for now keeping region throttles in place for 2 hours.
vikram: closing loop — provisioner error rate down to 0.8% after actions. keeping watch for next 2 hours. :thumbsup:
